description: A common fungal disease caused by Alternaria solani affecting leaves, stems, and fruits of tomatoes.
symptoms: Dark brown to black spots with concentric rings (target-like pattern) on older leaves.
Yellow halos surrounding leaf lesions.
Premature leaf drop leading to sunscald on fruits.
generalInformation: Thrives in warm, humid weather and spreads via rain splashes and wind.
prevention: Ensure proper plant spacing for good air circulation.
Water at the base of the plant using drip irrigation to keep foliage dry.
Apply copper-based or bio-fungicide sprays upon early detection.
Practice 2-3 year crop rotation with non-solanaceous crops.

description: A devastating water mold infection caused by Phytophthora infestans that can quickly destroy entire tomato crops.
symptoms: Large, irregularly shaped water-soaked lesions on leaves and stems.
White fungal fuzzy growth on leaf undersides in high humidity.
Rapidly turning dark brown and collapsing plant tissue.
generalInformation: The same pathogen that caused the Irish Potato Famine; spreads rapidly during cool, wet conditions.
prevention: Destroy and discard infected plant debris immediately (do not compost).
Avoid overhead watering and minimize leaf wetness duration.
Select certified disease-free transplants and blight-resistant cultivars.

description: Vibrant, healthy tomato foliage with optimal chlorophyll levels and no visible pathogen damage.
symptoms: Deep green uniform leaf coloration.
Firm, upright leaf stems without spots or discoloration.
Even leaf margins and active healthy growth.
generalInformation: Healthy tomato foliage supports strong photosynthetic activity for high fruit yield.
prevention: Maintain consistent soil moisture and balanced N-P-K fertilization.
Scout foliage weekly for early signs of pests or disease.

description: Fungal infection caused by Alternaria solani causing target-spot lesions on potato canopies.
symptoms: Small dark spots enlarging into concentric circular lesions.
Lower canopy foliage yellowing and dying early.
Dark sunken lesions on potato tuber skin.
generalInformation: Often affects plants under stress or lacking nitrogen and potassium.
prevention: Maintain optimal crop nutrition and irrigation to avoid plant stress.
Apply protective fungicides prior to canopy closure in high risk seasons.
Harvest tubers after vines are completely dead to minimize skin infection.

description: Highly contagious disease caused by Phytophthora infestans capable of rotting foliage and tubers.
symptoms: Pale green to dark water-soaked spots rapidly turning purplish-brown.
White downy mildew on the underside of leaves in humid mornings.
Tubers with dry brown granular rot beneath skin.
generalInformation: Spread by windborne sporangia across several miles in damp conditions.
prevention: Plant certified disease-free seed tubers.
Hill soil well over developing tubers to prevent spores washing down.
Eliminate cull piles and volunteer potato plants near fields.

description: Vigorous potato foliage exhibiting strong vegetative development.
symptoms: Lush green compound leaves.
No spotting, wilting, or stem lesions.
Uniform canopy density.
generalInformation: Indicates optimal nutrient balance and favorable growing environment.
prevention: Maintain adequate soil drainage and regular monitoring routine.

description: Airborne fungal disease caused by Puccinia sorghi producing rust-colored pustules on corn leaves.
symptoms: Oval to elongate cinnamon-brown pustules scattered across both leaf surfaces.
Pustules rupture epidermal tissue releasing reddish-brown powdery spores.
Chlorosis and premature leaf death in severe cases.
generalInformation: Fugitive spores blow northward each spring; favored by moderate temperatures (16–25°C) and high humidity.
prevention: Plant rust-resistant corn hybrid varieties.
Foliar fungicides may be applied if rust reaches upper leaves before tasseling.

description: Healthy corn leaves with clear parallel venation and strong photosynthetic vigor.
symptoms: Clean linear blades without pustules or lesions.
Rich deep green color along midrib and margins.
Sturdy stalk connection and clean leaf collars.
generalInformation: Healthy corn canopies maximize solar interception for grain fill.
prevention: Practice balanced nitrogen management and weed control.

description: Fungal infection by Venturia inaequalis causing velvety olive-green to black spots on apple foliage and fruit.
symptoms: Dull olive-green velvety lesions with feathery borders on young leaves.
Leaves become distorted, puckered, and turn yellow before dropping.
Scabby, cracked lesions on apple skin.
generalInformation: Overwinters in fallen leaves and releases ascospores during spring rain events.
prevention: Rake and destroy or compost fallen autumn leaves thoroughly.
Prune trees annually to enhance canopy sunlight and air drying.
Use preventive organic sprays or resistant apple varieties like Enterprise or Liberty.

description: Healthy apple tree foliage without blotches, curling, or mildew.
symptoms: Glossy, emerald-green serrated leaves.
Smooth leaf underside with no fungal coating.
Vigorous shoot extension.
generalInformation: Reflects excellent orchard sanitation and canopy management.
prevention: Maintain regular pruning and seasonal dormant oil treatments.

description: Fungal disease caused by Guignardia bidwellii affecting all green parts of grapevines.
symptoms: Small reddish-brown circular spots on leaves with tiny black pycnidia dots.
Infected berries shrivel into hard, black, wrinkled mummies.
Dark sunken cankers on green shoots.
generalInformation: One of the most destructive grape diseases in warm, wet viticultural regions.
prevention: Remove and destroy all mummified berries during winter pruning.
Open up the vine canopy with leaf pulling to reduce humidity.
Apply protective bio-fungicides from early bud break through fruit set.

description: Vibrant grapevine leaves and clean canes with high photosynthetic efficiency.
symptoms: Broad, distinctively lobed leaves with bright green luster.
Clean leaf veins and supple petioles.
Unblemished cluster development.
generalInformation: Optimal canopy architecture supports premium berry ripening and sugar accumulation.
prevention: Maintain regular canopy training and soil moisture control.
